questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Wanting to get away and to be on my own

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to get far away and to a really different culture. Then I narrowed it down to a few places that also had interesting academic programs in my field.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Actually quite easy - although its hard to avoid all confusion. The school communicated well in English. Choosing classes was really tricky though.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I would have loved some more information about their way of choosing classes. I was not giving all the wishes I had upon arrival, so I needed to apply for alternative classes via their standard function for all students. Not easy when you dont know it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy yes, but very expensive. I can really recommend staying with Weave though - tiny rooms, but a lot of exchange students and nice common areas. But again: Expensive!!!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus housing is FAR AWAY in the village of Ma-on Shan. This means that you are far away from the city, and trains stop running. I can really recommend to find your own place and safe up for the cost, since this will allow you to actually enjoy the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I'm not sure I fully remember, but we were told to meet up at an office (a little hard to find) to register and to get an ID card.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I ask employees and students for help finding my way. Worked nicely.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed at the end, but again it was a bit difficult. Most I registered in from home though.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the process, then you will be fine. Application is analog though, so be in good time to send it by mail. I teamed up with other danish students to split the cost of sending it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My creative classes were amazing, the other ones not that great to be honest. Definitely a lower level than Denmark.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: they seemed easier than my BA classes at home.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Lectures and group work - in almost all classes there were group works, and you were expected to figure out a group yourself.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Photography, Documentary 1, Movies and psychology, Hong Kong History, culture and society & Principles of Public Relations.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely my photography and documentary classes - AMAZING teachers.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: In general Hong Kong is an expensive city, so going out for drinks is costly - but you can find great happy hour offers in a lot of places.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Drinks were more! Buying full meals at restaurants were cheaper than I thought. Food in the supermarket more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot, but I didnt take part in any though.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Its not related to school, but the city as amazing nature all the way around it - go on hikes, camp at beaches and rent a boat with friends for a daytime party!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Shenzhen is wild - go clubbing but bring someone speaking chinese is you can.. I also visited Macao, definitely an experience. Would have loved to go more into China, there are so many BEAUTIFUL places nearby. In general plane tickets are really cheap from Hong Kong so plan after taking weekendtrips - Korea, Taiwan, Japan is not that far away! Safe up for this.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it interesting to get to know the culture, but it was diffivult to get to know locals. I had group work with some, but we stayed professional. Most of my free time was spend with other exchange students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Group work is a good starting point

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I was acutally shocked how safe I felt. Hong Kong is highly surveillanced and even though some might dislike it, it was a joy as a woman travilling on your own to feel this safe walking the streets alone, even at night!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and the spirituality!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: stay away from the dorms, safe up for weekend trips - and don't stress about school. All it will reflect on your papers are a pass/no pass, so enjoy your time away from home!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think I said it all.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I meet, the parties and the hikes!!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Eating meat (i was vegetarian before, that was not possible here)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
